### 5.5. Propositional Interpolation

It is possible to compute interpolants using models and cores \[[13](#chocklerim12 "Hana Chockler, Alexander Ivrii, and Arie Matsliah. 
Computing interpolants without proofs.")\]. A procedure that computes an interpolant ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,) for formulas ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,), ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,), where ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,) is unsatisfiable proceeds by initializing ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,) and saturating a state ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,) with respect to the rules:

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The partial interpolant ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,) produced by pogo satisfies ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,). It terminates when ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,). The condition ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,) ensures that the algorithm makes progress and suggests using an implicant ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,) of ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,) in each iteration. Such an implicant can be obtained from a model for ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,).

```
def mk_lit(m, x):
    if is_true(m.eval(x)):
       return x
    else:
       return Not(x)

def pogo(A, B, xs):   
    while sat == A.check():
       m = A.model()
       L = [mk_lit(m, x) for x in xs]
       if unsat == B.check(L):
          notL = Not(And(B.unsat_core()))
          yield notL
          A.add(notL)
       else:
          print("expecting unsat")
          break
```
